units.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python reads and writes 3D scenes in .3mf, .fbx, .glb, .gltf, .obj, and .stl formats. It constructs scenes using Scene, creates entities such as Mesh via PolygonBuilder, and manages transforms, materials, and animation clips through its public API.
It reads .3mf, .dae, .fbx, .glb, .gltf, .obj, and .stl files using Scene.open() with automatic format detection from the file extension or an explicit FileFormat.
It exports scenes to .3mf, .glb, .gltf, and .stl formats using Scene.save() with format-specific SaveOptions subclasses for coordinate flipping, unit scaling, and compression settings.

It builds and traverses scene graphs using Node.create_child_node(), Node.add_entity(), and Node.child_nodes, with each node carrying an independent Transform that stores translation, rotation, and scale.

It constructs and edits mesh geometry through Mesh.control_points, Mesh.create_polygon(), and Mesh.polygons, or by converting parameterized primitives like Box and Sphere using their to_mesh() method.
It assigns LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes, setting diffuse, specular, emissive, and PBR albedo/metallic/roughness color and factor properties directly.
It supports keyframe animation using AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence, and stores skeletal bind-pose data with Pose.
This example creates a box with a blue Lambert material and saves it as a glTF file.
This example creates a sphere with a metallic PBR material and saves it as an STL file.
The following examples demonstrate common workflows: creating and exporting meshes, inspecting scene graphs, and converting primitives.
Create a mesh with a PBR material and export to glTF.
Open a glTF file and walk its scene graph.
Build a triangle mesh and export to ASCII STL.
Convert a Box primitive to a mesh and count control points.
Build a cube mesh and export to uncompressed 3MF.

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python provides the aspose.threed.Scene class as the primary entry point for loading and saving 3D scenes built from Node objects, each of which can hold a Transform, an optional Entity, and one or more Material instances. The aspose.threed.FileFormat class supports detection and dispatch for multiple 3D file formats, and the aspose.threed.Mesh class provides polygonal geometry representation.
The Mesh class exposes control_points and edges for geometry data, provides Mesh.create_polygon() for polygon construction, and supports spatial queries via Mesh.get_bounding_box().
The aspose.threed.shading module provides classes for physically based rendering workflows, including material types that support diffuse, specular, metallic, and roughness properties.
It adds broader proprietary-format support (PDF, PLY, USD, and more), rendering, and advanced mesh operations that this FOSS build leaves unimplemented.
